newsitem.title: MALTA: Levy urges Mideast negotiations with no preconditions.
newsitem.headline: Levy urges Mideast negotiations with no preconditions.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy, responding to Palestinian condemnation of his country's policies, called on Tuesday for negotiations to be restarted, "without preconditions, without threats".

Levy told foreign ministers from the European Union and 12 Mediterranean partners in Malta they were meeting with "storm clouds over the Middle East peace process" but that the march to peace was irreversible.

He made no reference, however, to the cause of the latest crisis, the widely-condemned decision of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to start building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem a month ago.
Since then, Israelis and Palestinians have clashed almost daily.

Earlier on Tuesday, in the same forum, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat accused the Israeli government of a fierce campaign of settlement to demolish the bridges of confidence between the two sides.
Levy said there were serious threats to the peace process but Israel's commitment to peace was "beyond doubt" and must be based on "cooperation, confidence and trust".

He accused critics of the Jewish state of ignoring all its earlier efforts for peace and said "undue pressure" was being brought to bear on his government, an apparent reference to U.N. resolutions last month on Israel's policies .
"We remain firmly convinced of the fact that we have to jointly march to a peaceful resolution," Levy said. "The road towards peace is an irreversible process. There is no alternative."
Without naming the Palestinians, Levy said statements against Israel created a dangerous climate, linking it to a Tel Aviv bombing last month in which three women and the bomber died.

"We would like the Palestinian Authority to broadcast, to publicise an unequivocably clear message against terrorism, refuting terrorism, returning to the dialogue, making the peace objective a common goal. That I believe is the only single remedy," he said.
He added: "A code of conduct will have to be elaborated, and further work carried out with a view to bringing about that lasting peace which we strive towards."
